newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp seen holding 30 pct of Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Krupp seen holding 30 pct of Thyssen.

text.p: German steel maker Krupp has secured around 30 percent of Thyssen AG's capital in safekeeping with institutional investors as part of its efforts to take over its rival, a German newspaper reported.

In an advance copy of a report to appear on Friday, the Handelsblatt economic daily cited banking sources and said that Krupp was still interested in taking control of its larger rival and had secured a 15 billion mark credit line from banks.
Talks that began on Thursday between the two companies to discuss the merger of each company's steel divisions were just the first step in broader talks about a full merger, the paper wrote.

A Krupp spokesman declined to comment on the report. He repeated the company's position that should the 8-day talks with Thyssen about a steel merger not produce any results, the company would resume its efforts to acquire Thyssen shares on the stock market.

Earlier this week, Krupp offered 435 marks per share to Thyssen shareholders, a 25 percent premium over the closing share price from Monday. It then put the offer on ice after Thyssen agreed to discuss merging their steel operations.
